title: Program Architect
html:
Copado

September 2021 - June 2023

As a Program Architect at Copado, my mission was to help some of the world's largest organisations improve the way they delivered change through Salesforce.

Every customer faced different challenges. Some struggled with inefficient release processes, while others needed a strategic vision for how DevOps could support long-term business goals. My role was to investigate the current state, identify opportunities for improvement, and build practical roadmaps for transformation.

One engagement involved a major financial institution where I identified technology and process challenges that were creating significant operational overhead every month. By helping define a new DevOps approach and guiding transition activities, those inefficiencies were removed while improving the consistency of platform releases.

I regularly acted as a trusted advisor to engineering teams, development partners, and senior stakeholders. Through coaching, planning, and technical leadership, I helped organisations establish stronger delivery practices and gain greater value from their investment in Salesforce.

Beyond customer engagements, I developed reusable solutions for use in release pipelines that could be adopted across multiple projects, improving consistency for both customers and consulting teams.

My work and passion for cultural transformation in technology eventually led to an invitation to deliver a keynote presentation on the importance of people and culture within successful DevOps programmes.

Skills gained: DevOps Strategy, Salesforce Delivery, Enterprise Consulting, Stakeholder Management, Product Architecture, Organisational Change.

title: Service Design & Transition Manager
html:
Domestic & General

February 2020 - September 2021

I re-joined Domestic & General at a pivotal moment in the company's history. The organisation was preparing to enter a major new market in the United States, and technology would play a crucial role in making that expansion successful.

My mission was twofold. First, I was asked to lead the Service Management workstream supporting the expansion programme. Second, I took on responsibilities as a Solution Architect, helping shape the technology foundations that would support the business as it entered a new territory.

One of the first challenges was defining how services would be delivered in this new operating environment. Working closely with technology leaders and delivery partners, I helped create a target operating model and capability model for Service Management. These blueprints provided clarity around responsibilities, delivery approaches, and the partnerships required to support long-term success.

As plans evolved, I designed a Service Management Blueprint that embraced modern DevSecOps principles. Rather than relying on traditional governance-heavy processes, the focus was on enabling teams to deliver securely, efficiently, and at scale. The result was an approach that balanced control with agility and supported the fast-paced demands of a growing business, maintaing local control along with light-touch global oversight.

To bring this vision to life, I led the selection and implementation of key tools that would form the backbone of the engineering ecosystem. This included technologies such as Jira, GitHub, Copado, Confluence, and ServiceNow, supporting both AWS and Salesforce platforms. Together, these tools formed an integrated DevSecOps toolchain capable of supporting development, operations, governance, and collaboration.

I also led the solution design for a low-touch onboarding capability for employees in the United States. By leveraging Microsoft Autopilot and direct-to-door device fulfilment, new joiners could receive and configure their devices with minimal manual intervention, improving both efficiency and employee experience.

Throughout my time at Domestic & General, I worked closely with teams across the organisation, coaching colleagues on effective Service Management practices and helping ensure that solutions were designed with security, scalability, and reliability in mind.

The role reinforced a lesson that has followed me throughout my career: successful transformation is not just about technology. It is about creating the right operating model, empowering people, and building services that enable the business to achieve its goals.

Skills gained: Service Design, Solution Architecture, DevSecOps, AWS, Salesforce, ServiceNow, Operating Model Design, Technology Strategy, Service Management, Digital Transformation.

title: Service Architect
html:
Dentsu Aegis Network

May 2018 - February 2019

I earned a promotion to Service Architect at a critical moment in Dentsu's technology transformation journey. The organisation was rapidly evolving, bringing critical services back in-house while simultaneously building new digital capabilities for a global business operating across many regions and brands.

My first major challenge was leading the modernisation of the company's ServiceNow platform. The platform was heavily customised, widely used across the business, and considered too important to fail. By bringing together the right people, focusing on outcomes, and maintaining a relentless attention to detail, I led the successful upgrade of the platform in just five weeks, delivering the project three weeks ahead of schedule while maintaining operational stability.

Beyond individual projects, I was responsible for helping shape the future direction of service technology across the organisation. Working closely with senior leadership, I developed a ServiceNow product roadmap aligned to the strategic priorities of the Global CTO. This roadmap provided clarity, direction, and focus for multiple transformation initiatives while balancing the operational needs of teams across the business.

Recognising that successful transformation depends on people as much as technology, I helped establish a new Business Analysis capability by recruiting and mentoring junior team members and building a peering capability with existing senior resources to provide a stronger pipeline of talent and enabling stronger engagement between technical teams and business stakeholders. Within weeks, these new team members were making valuable contributions to ongoing programmes.

As the organisation's Service Management authority within architecture discussions, I worked across a wide variety of initiatives to ensure systems were designed with operational excellence in mind. I published technology standards covering Service Management, Event Management, Monitoring, and Collaboration platforms, creating a consistent foundation that could be adopted globally.

What I enjoyed most about this role was helping teams see the bigger picture. By combining architecture, strategy, governance, and delivery, I was able to contribute to a transformation that extended far beyond any single platform.

Skills gained: Service Architecture, ServiceNow, Technology Strategy, Enterprise Governance, Team Leadership, Business Analysis, Service Management, Platform Modernisation.

title: IT Service Architect & Service Designer
html:
Harrods

February 2019 - February 2020

When I joined Harrods, the organisation was embarking on an ambitious transformation programme targeting the replacement of an ageing and costly eCommerce platform while modernising the business capabilities that supported it.

My role was to ensure that new technology could be introduced successfully without disrupting the first-class customer experience that the Harrods brand is known for. To achieve this, I established a Service Design and Transition framework that provided structure, consistency, and confidence during a period of rapid change.

One of my most significant contributions was designing the service model for the new eCommerce capability. This involved defining processes, selecting Service Management approaches, and creating clear interactions between internal teams and strategic delivery partners. By building these foundations early, the organisation was able to scale delivery while maintaining operational control.

As the transformation accelerated, I identified opportunities to automate manual processes that were slowing teams down. Improvements to Change and Incident communications reduced administrative effort and enabled faster, more reliable collaboration between operations and development teams.

I also helped guide several high-profile service introductions. A notable example was the implementation of Workday, where I designed an Early Life Support model that brought together colleagues from IT, Payroll, and HR in a collaboration that had not been experienced before. This ensured issues could be identified and resolved quickly during the critical launch period.

Recognising the growing demand for governance and service introduction expertise, I recruited and led a Service Design and Transition team. Together we supported more than 50 live projects, helping ensure that change was introduced in a controlled and sustainable manner.

Towards the end of my tenure, I project managed key aspects of the migration to the new eCommerce platform. This included defining cutover plans and establishing a cross-functional Command Centre that coordinated activities across multiple teams, ensuring a smooth transition to the new environment.

Looking back, this role strengthened my ability to balance technology, people, and process during large-scale transformation programmes. It demonstrated how effective service design can enable organisations to move quickly while maintaining stability and trust.

Skills gained: Service Design, Digital Transformation, eCommerce Platforms, Team Leadership, Process Automation, Service Introduction, ITIL, Programme Delivery, Change Management.

title: Principal Platform Engineer
html:
London Stock Exchange Group

June 2023 - Current

At LSEG, my mission evolved from transforming DevOps practices into building and leading engineering capabilities at enterprise scale.

I joined following a successful consulting engagement, taking on responsibility for transforming the Salesforce engineering capability supporting the Sales & Service platforms underpinning a £4bn revenue engine. The challenge was to dramatically increase the organisation's ability to deliver change while maintaining the stability expected of a highly critical enterprise platform.

The first quest was release engineering. The existing capability supported around 180 developers but was delivering only 12 releases a year. I transformed the operating model and engineering capability, increasing this to more than 70 releases annually while maintaining product stability.

Building the right team was central to the transformation. I recruited and established an in-house DevOps capability of 14 engineers, bringing critical expertise into the organisation and creating the foundations for sustainable engineering delivery.

My remit then expanded into Quality Engineering, where I led a 50-person capability supporting 20 engineering squads through a team of managers. I helped drive automated test coverage from 70% to more than 85%, strengthening quality and confidence across increasingly frequent releases.

As LSEG pivoted to wider adoption of AI-assisted development, I saw opportunities to embed AI into development cycles of our teams while maintaining close engineering oversight, code review and quality controls, one resource-constrained squad was able to reduce features that previously took months to build down to days.

As the transformation progressed, my role expanded beyond Salesforce into cross-platform engineering. I began leading capability across AWS and other emerging platforms, including a new team of three engineers working on platforms being built from the ground up.

I remained deliberately hands-on throughout this growth, continuing to contribute to technical and architectural decisions and staying close to the technology while leading increasingly large and complex engineering capabilities.

The transformation also created significant commercial value. By identifying opportunities to build strategic capabilities in-house rather than purchase commercial products, I delivered more than £500k in annual cost savings while aligning investment with the wider engineering strategy.

My impact was recognised through selection for LSEG's Global Enterprise Engineering programme, chosen from hundreds of applicants to join a small cohort focused on enterprise-level engineering leadership. I have also consistently received the highest available performance rating and been recognised as a top contributor throughout my tenure.

Skills gained: Engineering Leadership, Team Building, Recruitment, Platform Engineering, Product Engineering, DevOps, Quality Engineering, Salesforce, AWS, AI-Assisted Development, Engineering Strategy, Technical Leadership, Cost Optimisation, Organisational Transformation.

title: Autonomous Dev Agent Pipeline
html:
I built a proof of concept to test theories about the potential benefits and costs of a self-directed software development pipeline, starting from Jira ticket through to merge request.

  • Orchestrated with LangGraph, tool calls bound via LangChain
  • LLM inference using Azure AI Foundry with the ability to leverage different models in each phase
  • Human-in-the-loop gates with inputs and overrides through a custom React interface
  • Temporal for durable workflow state, PostgreSQL for story state, Qdrant for RAG
  • Covers spec generation, planning, coding, review, test execution, docs, and deployment to a Salesforce org ready for human review
  • Full cost overview per-requirement and per-phase by tracking token usage and running a pricing engine to help answer the question of 'how much does this cost to deliver?'

From this project I took away several learnings, not least thinking about when not to use non-deterministic and potentially expensive LLM calls and instead sticking to deterministic evaluations instead.

title: DIY Camera/Radar Launch Monitor
html:
A homebrew launch monitor, built to track a 20-handicap golf game one range session at a time.

  • Camera-based capture using the Arducam B0332 OV9281 120fps camera
  • Python, OpenCV, and Pygame for the capture and analysis pipeline through to display on a rudimentry UI
  • Feeds a longitudinal dataset used to spot swing patterns over time on a per-club basis

Building this project helped me to learn more about mapping co-ordinates in images, analysing image differences in a pipeline, and presenting and persisting outputs.
